_why:
Fifteen edges resting on three congressional hearing transcripts, all three downloaded from govinfo and read in full: CHRG-118hhrg53022 (House Oversight, 26 July 2023), CHRG-118hhrg57440 (13 November 2024) and CHRG-119hhrg61718 (9 September 2025).

Sourcing an edge means reading the document the note rests on, and three notes turned out to assert more than their transcript does.

maxwell-frost -> ryan-graves said Frost 'asked Graves how NASA research might influence commercial aviation safety' and that 'Graves pointed to NASA's Aviation Safety' reporting system. Neither is in Frost's exchange. Frost asked Graves exactly two questions - about the importance of scientists on his advisory board, and how Congress might facilitate partnerships between the scientific community and the UAP focus groups within government - and Graves answered by citing the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics. The aviation-safety exchange in that hearing is Grothman's, not Frost's. Rewritten to the transcript.

klas-tv -> aawsap said Knapp testified he was asked to share the Russian Ministry of Defense papers with BAASS and the DIA and did so, and that AAWSAP assembled a translation team. His ORAL testimony says he shared them with the Task Force, and describes Thread III and Colonel Boris Sokolov. The BAASS/DIA sharing is not in the printed hearing, which reproduces oral statements only - the written statements are held separately at docs.house.gov and are not in the CHRG document. The edge is tier 2, sourced to what Knapp did say on the record about AAWSAP, with the gap named.

klas-tv -> harry-reid said Reid was the first person Knapp told outside the KLAS newsroom about the 1989 Lazar story, beginning 'a private collaboration'. The transcript has Knapp reporting the Lazar story in 1989 and listing Reid among the dozens he has interviewed since, but not the 'first person told' sequence, which is again the written statement. Rewritten to the record.

The strongest item in the 2025 transcript is one the board should not lose: Knapp states on the record that 'Robert Bigelow and a trusted colleague from AAWSAP met with and negotiated with senior executives at Lockheed Martin and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that had been stashed away and protected at a facility in California. That material was not made here.' That is a custody allegation made under oath and it belongs in the klas-tv -> aawsap note.

sources.name: House Oversight and Accountability Committee hearing, 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency', 26 July 2023 (CHRG-118hhrg53022)

edges.note: Biggs put the 1997 Phoenix Lights case to Grusch directly - 'I am going to take you to specific instances around the Phoenix Valley because that is where I live' - and asked whether he knew anything beyond the official explanation of a military training range off Luke and the Barry Goldwater range. Grusch: 'Only what is in the public vernacular about it. That was outside the scope of my duties.'

Asked by Biggs whether the 2019 classification guidelines interfere with the government's ability to be transparent, Grusch answered: 'Yes, I am familiar with the UAP Task Force 2019 Security Classification guide. I think it is fair. I did actually help author that with the Director.' Biggs: 'Uh-oh. You got a bias then.' Grusch then characterised the practice rather than the guide - 'I will call it a lazy attitude about declassifying videos'. The witness co-authored the instrument he was being asked to criticise, and said so unprompted.

Frost told the hearing: 'In fact, I sit on the Science, Space and Technology Committee and when we were doing a hearing with the NASA Administrator, Bill Nelson, I asked, you know, why NASA needed to be fully funded. And there were many great reasons, but one of them was actually--had to do with UAPs.' He tied it forward to the NASA independent study team and to Harvard standing up the Galileo Project in 2021.

Frost asked Graves two questions: 'can you discuss the importance of seeking scientists to sit on your advisory board?' and 'how might Congress help to facilitate partnerships between the scientific community and the UAP focus groups within government?' Graves answered that this 'is going to be a scientific problem, and not only that, it is also an engineering problem', and pointed to his work with the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics to stand up a UAP integration committee.

Chairman Grothman recognised Biggs, who questioned Grusch, Graves and Fravor on misdirection by the government regarding UAP, the 1997 Phoenix Lights, and the 2019 UAP classification guidelines. He is recorded in the transcript as a member of the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.

Frost used his round on the scientific and stigma dimension: NASA's independent study team, the Galileo Project, whether military pilots feeling empowered to speak had shifted scientific research goals, and how Congress might connect scientists to the government's UAP work. He closed: 'I think it is important that we keep our top scientific minds focused on this issue and look for ways to increase collaboration.'

sources.name: House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets hearing, 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection', 9 September 2025 (CHRG-119hhrg61718)

edges.note: Knapp opened his sworn statement: 'I am George Knapp, chief investigative reporter at KLAS-TV in Las Vegas. I began my pursuit of this weird mystery way back in 1987, and for 38 years, I have always approached this as a news story. It is not a matter of faith or belief to me.' The witness list gives him as 'Mr. George Knapp, UAP Journalist'; Chairwoman Luna's introduction dates his arrival at KLAS to 1981 and the chief investigative reporter post to 1995.

sources.name: House Oversight Task Force hearing, 9 September 2025 (CHRG-119hhrg61718)

edges.note: The transcript lists 'Mr. Joe Spielberger (Minority Witness), Senior Policy Counsel, Project on Government Oversight'. His statement opens 'Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and Task Force members' and describes POGO as 'a nonpartisan independent watchdog organization that investigates and exposes waste, corruption, abuse of power, and when the government fails to serve the public or silences those who report wrongdoing.' He appeared as the minority witness, on whistleblower protection rather than on the phenomenon.

sources.name: House Oversight Task Force hearing, 9 September 2025 (CHRG-119hhrg61718)

edges.note: Spielberger's testimony is addressed to 'Chairwoman Luna, Ranking Member Crockett, and Task Force members' and lays out a legislative agenda for protecting UAP whistleblowers. Luna convened and chaired the hearing and is recorded throughout the transcript as presiding.

sources.name: House Oversight Task Force hearing, 9 September 2025 (CHRG-119hhrg61718)

edges.note: Knapp named Lacatski on the record as one of the people he has interviewed: 'There is a guy named Dr. James Lacatski, who was a career scientist with the Defense Intelligence Agency, who was the guy who initiated a program called AAWSAP, Advanced Aerospace Weapons Systems Application Program, which is, as far as we know, the largest acknowledged UFO program ever funded by the U.S. Government.'

sources.name: House Oversight Task Force hearing, 9 September 2025 (CHRG-119hhrg61718)

edges.note: Knapp told the Task Force that after reporting the Bob Lazar / S-4 story in 1989 he 'interviewed dozens of other people' over the years, and named the list: 'They include Senator Harry Reid; Senator Howard Cannon, also of Nevada; a guy named Al O'Donnell, who was the first general manager of EG&G in Nevada... There is a guy named Dr. James Lacatski.' The printed hearing reproduces oral statements only, so the sequence in which Knapp first approached Reid sits in his written statement at docs.house.gov and is not asserted here.

sources.name: House Oversight Task Force hearing, 9 September 2025 (CHRG-119hhrg61718)

edges.note: Knapp's custody allegation, made under oath: 'I have confirmed on the record that Robert Bigelow and a trusted colleague from AAWSAP met with and negotiated with senior executives at Lockheed Martin and hammered out a deal wherein Bigelow's company, BAASS, would receive a quantity of unusual material that had been stashed away and protected at a facility in California. That material was not made here.' On the Russia files he testified that he obtained documents and interviews from Soviet defence officials in the early 1990s and has 'now shared with this Task Force' - the printed hearing carries no statement that he shared them with BAASS or the DIA, which is why this is tier 2. It is an allegation by a named witness, not a documented transfer.

sources.name: Joint House Oversight subcommittee hearing, 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth', 13 November 2024 (CHRG-118hhrg57440)

edges.note: The transcript lists 'Mr. Michael Shellenberger, Founder of Public' as one of four witnesses, alongside Rear Admiral Timothy Gallaudet, Luis Elizondo and Michael Gold. His statement opens 'Chairwoman Mace, Chairman Grothman, Ranking Member Connolly, Ranking Member Garcia, Members of the Subcommittees' - a joint sitting of two subcommittees.

sources.name: Joint House Oversight subcommittee hearing, 13 November 2024 (CHRG-118hhrg57440)

edges.note: Shellenberger brought the Immaculate Constellation allegation to Congress, arguing 'there is a growing body of evidence that the U.S. Government is not being transparent about what it knows about unidentified anomalous phenomena and that elements within the military and the IC are in violation of their constitutional duty to notify Congress of their operations.' The name appears seventeen times across the printed hearing.

sources.name: Joint House Oversight subcommittee hearing, 13 November 2024 (CHRG-118hhrg57440)

edges.note: The hearing's own index of documents records the route the material took into the record: 'Report, Pentagon, ``Immaculate Constellation``; submitted by Rep. Mace.' Mace chaired the sitting - Shellenberger's statement opens by addressing her as Chairwoman - and it was she, not the witness, who entered the document.
